solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Properly equipped lad fixed up, you might say

indicators.note: 'you might say' asks us to judge the words by how they are spoken rather than how they are written

parts.note: Will is a boy's name, so a lad; to fix up a meal is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A boy has been kitted out properly for something, as someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Lad is crossword shorthand for any boy's name; WILL PREPARED, said quickly, comes out close to WELL-PREPARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with all the gear and readiness needed for a task is ready and fully kitted out in advance.

clue.text: In combat, everyone loves a jumper

indicators.note: 'In' says the word just before is surrounded by the one that comes after

parts.note: combat is war
everyone is all
love is zero in tennis, so O; two of them

explanation.surface: Everybody in a war adores a warm sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' wants to be a British sweater, which fits the soldiers; here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaroo is a large Australian kangaroo species, an animal that moves by hopping on powerful hind legs.

clue.text: A river between two lakes forming bay

indicators.note: something lying between two things is flanked by them, one on each side

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake; two of them
taken as written
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A river runs between two lakes and creates a bay on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a stretch of coastline; it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay tree, whose leaves flavour stews, is also called the sweet laurel, Laurus nobilis.

clue.text: One pushing and one riding a bike, we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' tells the solver to go by the spoken sound of the phrase before it

parts.note: someone riding a bicycle pedals, so is a pedaller

explanation.surface: Someone is shoving a bicycle while another person rides it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing' suggests pushing a bike, but it means selling wares, as a pusher does.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar travels about hawking small goods, and to push goods is to sell them insistently.

clue.text: Skin split by broken arm, I cry for first aid

indicators.note: a thing split by something has that other thing wedged into the gap

parts.note: to skin fruit is to pare it

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured person whose skin is torn and arm broken cries out for medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: Primary care is the first point of medical help, from a GP or nurse, before any specialist treatment.

clue.text: Immaculate dress, as Spooner might say now

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

parts.note: immaculate is spotless white; to dress is to array; swap the first sounds

explanation.surface: Someone wants a spotless outfit at once.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the W and R sounds of WHITE ARRAY gives RIGHT AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something immediately, without any delay, is doing it at this very moment.

clue.text: LOCO DERAILS — 1 PM

indicators.note: loco is slang for crazy, so the letters beside it go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A headline: a locomotive comes off the rails at one in the afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LOCO' looks like a railway engine and 'PM' like the time of day; PM is Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli served twice as British Prime Minister for the Conservatives in Queen Victoria's reign.

clue.text: King opens shop cooking sea food

indicators.note: something that opens another goes inside it, prising it apart

parts.note: a plant is a factory or workshop
K is the chess abbreviation for king
food that is cooking is on the stove

explanation.surface: A monarch opens a shop where seafood is being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea food' is not a dish for people but the food of the sea itself, eaten by whales and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are tiny drifting organisms that form the base of the marine diet for fish and whales.

clue.text: The harmful part of killing

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the harmful thing, an ill

indicators.note: 'part of' says the letters are a piece taken from inside the next word

parts.note: sits inside the word, after the K

explanation.surface: A grim observation that the damaging element of any killing is plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun: an ill is a harm or evil, as in 'the ills of society'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an ill is a misfortune or source of harm, something damaging or bad.

clue.text: Try to hold love down, likely to fail

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to have a fling is to have a try
zero in tennis
down means below, under

explanation.surface: Advice to keep your affection suppressed, since it will probably end badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A floundering business or person is struggling helplessly and seems headed for collapse.

clue.text: Domestic fowl keeping or returning waterfowl

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a hen is a farmyard bird

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A farmyard chicken is kept, or comes back, alongside water birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Note 'or' is a letter source here, not a choice between two things.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes, loosely counted among water birds.

clue.text: Tramp and sailor about to get lower tax

indicators.note: 'about' as in turning about: the whole run of letters faces the other way

parts.note: to tramp is to pace
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A vagrant and a sailor turn up to get a cut in their taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rate-capping was the British government's limit on local property taxes, the rates, in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate-cap a council was to impose a ceiling on its local property tax, keeping the charge down.

clue.text: Return much worried, after a divorce?

indicators.note: 'after' places the last piece behind the earlier ones in the answer

parts.note: a means per, as in five pounds a head
to divorce is to sever
what worried you was eating you

explanation.surface: After a divorce, someone keeps coming back to fret about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the hardest piece: it stands for per; ATE is worried, as in 'what's eating you?'
explanation.definitionFit: To perseverate is to repeat a word, thought or action compulsively, going back to it over and over.

clue.text: Look after guys in judo area preparing to fight again

parts.note: to rear children is to look after them

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: judo is fought on a mat
guys are men

explanation.surface: Someone tends the fighters on the judo mat as they get ready for the next bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmament is the process of a nation equipping itself with weapons once more for war.

clue.text: Owns houses right behind hotel, sounds unhappy

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside

parts.note: to own is to have

indicators.note: behind sets the earlier piece after the next one in the order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
one's behind is one's rump
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A property owner keeps houses right behind a hotel and complains about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' is not a position: it is a backside, RUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to clear the throat or grunt in a way that shows disapproval or displeasure.

clue.text: With old Asian doctor is new analytical method

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters before it are remade in a new order

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A therapy technique developed with help from an old Asian physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is used twice: once as fodder, once as the link to the definition; only the first 'is' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Word association is a psychoanalytic technique in which a patient replies to prompts with the first word that springs to mind.

clue.text: Google finds money to acquire English oil company

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: wages are money earned
E is the abbreviation for English
BP, formerly British Petroleum, is an oil company

explanation.surface: A business story: the search giant raises cash to buy a British oil firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' looks like a verb, but 'Google finds' is a noun phrase: the things a search turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: A search engine's results are links to online documents, the sites it turns up for a query.

clue.text: Doctor wrong to lance lip infection

indicators.note: to lance is to pierce, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the lip of a cup is its rim

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic mistakenly lances a sore on a patient's lip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician; it is a verb meaning to tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a contagious fungal skin disease, despite its name not caused by any worm.

clue.text: Shot, not great but accurate

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so the letters following are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports pundit judges a strike: not a great one, but it found its mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like the strike being judged; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something right on the bullseye has hit exactly what was aimed at, precisely as intended.

clue.text: Playwright's gift to people at party

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or gift
ravers are partygoers

explanation.surface: A dramatist presents something to the guests at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces such as Rookery Nook.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Travers was an English dramatist famous for the farces staged at London's Aldwych Theatre in the 1920s.

clue.text: The end of Oasis, rubbish band

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
tripe is rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A music critic's verdict: the last of Oasis, a terrible group.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis was a 1990s British rock group, so 'band' looks musical; it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour on a surface, a line or strip of a different shade.

clue.text: Do two days on board train

indicators.note: being on board means inside a vessel, so the piece goes within the other

parts.note: a train of people is a file, a line
D is the abbreviation for day; two of them

explanation.surface: An instruction to spend two days travelling on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is the slang verb meaning to cheat, not 'perform'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone, in slang, is to cheat or swindle them, and to fiddle is to cheat dishonestly.

clue.text: Just this Roman, and others around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so this piece encloses the other

parts.note: et al is the Latin abbreviation for and others
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A remark that only this Roman is present, along with a few companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are Latin: 'this' in a Roman's language is HIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and morally right, which is what an ethical act is.

clue.text: Like wife, I'm floating

parts.note: like means as
W is the abbreviation for wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband says he is floating along just as his wife is.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswim is a literary adjective for swimming or drifting in water, borne up by the liquid.

clue.text: Rodents or pigs I read about

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been reading about rodents, or maybe pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Prairie dogs are burrowing North American ground squirrels, which belong to the rodent order of mammals.

clue.text: Shell-like article held by monarch

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grasp

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A seashell-shaped object is in the keeping of a king or queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shell-like' is British slang for the ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer organ of hearing is called a shell-like in British slang because of its curled, conch shape.

clue.text: Pervert's son in trouble here

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to be in the mire is to be in trouble
S is the abbreviation for son
someone here is present

explanation.surface: A deviant's boy is in trouble and has turned up here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' is a verb, to distort, and the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervert the facts is to distort or twist them, giving a false account of what happened.
